_comment_scope: TERMINAL-HALT DEMO (BELLMAN_KNOWN_A_TERMINAL_HALT_DESIGN.md). A copy of embodied_pure_ddm_bellman.json tuned so the agent USUALLY reaches arrival undecided, visibly parks at the midpoint, and only then commits. Tuned by simulation against the solved boundary: A = 0.04, c = 0.354, c_e = 100, v = 0.15 gives T_max = 2.89 s, z_halt = 0.97, P(halt) ~ 0.82, median parking ~4-6 s (p90 ~ 14 s), then a ~90-degree turn and ~1.7 s travel to the chosen target. WHAT TO WATCH: the agent drives to the bisector foot, stops dead (v = 0, no rotation) while still undecided, sits there for seconds, then turns and drives off. Click the agent to open the Activity Inspector: the pure-DDM panel shows x(t) inside the collapsing +/-z(t), the dotted 'arrival' line, the +/-z_halt plateau past it, and the title switches to 'HALTED at midpoint' while parked.

environment._comment_time_limit: Halt durations are exponential-tailed (mean D(z_halt) - D(x_arrival) ~ 6 s from the midpoint); p99 of approach + halt + travel is ~35 s, so 60 s censors almost nothing. The runaway guard cap T_max + 10 D(z_halt) = 75.6 s sits above this limit, so an absurdly long halt is censored by the arena, not force-committed.

termination._comment: Proximity to a TARGET only: the midpoint is 0.25 m from either target, so the halt phase is never cut short by termination.

environment._comment_quality: A = |5.0 - 4.96| = 0.04, DELIBERATELY weak: over the short 2.89 s approach the evidence rarely resolves (drift * T_max = 0.12 against noise sd c*sqrt(T_max) = 0.60 and a boundary that starts at ~4), so ~82% of runs arrive undecided. The same weak drift is what makes the halt LAST: mean exit time D(z_halt) = (z_halt/A) tanh(k z_halt / 2) ~ 7.3 s from a central start.
environment._comment_geometry: Same 60-degree, 0.5 m layout as the bellman config: r0 = 0.433 m, half_L = 0.25 m. The faster v = 0.15 m/s is what shortens the approach to T_max = 2.89 s -- less time to decide en route is the main lever behind the high halt probability.

movable_0._comment_angular_velocity: deg/s. The commit happens AT the midpoint, where the chosen target sits ~90 degrees off the bisector heading; the minimum turn radius is v/omega and must be well under the 0.05 m termination radius or the agent orbits the target forever (the campaign config documents the measured orbit at 10 deg/s). 360 deg/s gives a 0.024 m radius.

embodied_pure_ddm._comment_n_sub: Sub-steps per 0.1 s tick: keeps the integration step c*sqrt(dt/n_sub) = 0.035 well under z_halt = 0.97, so the Inspector's x(t) trace is smooth and the crossing overshoot at commitment stays small.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_cost_ratio: c_e = 100 is what makes halting worthwhile: z_halt solves sinh(a)+a = (A/c)^2 c_e = 1.28, giving z_halt = 0.97 and a halt-commit accuracy of ~67% -- far better than the near-chance guess forced_choice would take at arrival with the same undecided x.

bellman._comment_T_max: null = r0/v = 2.89 s from the onset geometry.
bellman._comment_T_max_check_factor: The horizon check is a forced_choice diagnostic; under halt_sprt T_max is the physical arrival time and the check is recorded as skipped anyway (design doc Section 5, B3 note).
bellman._comment_N_t: dt = 1 ms over the 2.89 s horizon (the free boundary converges as O(sqrt(dt))).
bellman._comment_terminal: THE POINT OF THIS CONFIG: at arrival the agent halts at the midpoint (v = 0) and keeps integrating against the flat z_halt instead of force-committing. z(T_max) = z_halt = 0.97; watch pure_ddm_halted / halt_duration in the logs.
